summary: Implemented patch::write_chart_edits with a borrowed Write + ?Sized sink, complete preflight validation, direct borrowed byte emission, and typed validation/I/O errors. Added six integration tests covering all edit kinds and writer failure behavior.

commands.outcome: Passed; formatted the implementation and new integration tests.

Initial run failed: all 165 existing tests and 5 of 6 new integration tests passed; the payload test constructed a boxed concrete payload but attempted to downcast to the unboxed type. Corrected the test fixture to construct io::Error::other(Payload(42)) and capture the contained payload address.
Passed after correcting the test fixture.
Final run passed: 165 existing unit tests, 6 new integration tests, and 0 doctests; no ignored tests.

design_decisions: The writer is borrowed as &mut W with W: Write + ?Sized, supporting both concrete writers and trait objects without taking ownership, flushing, or closing.

Both output APIs use the existing Planner through a shared planning function, a shared sorting and full-span-validation helper, and a shared iterator of borrowed unchanged input and replacement slices. The streaming path does not create a complete input or output copy.

Bounds checks retain their original ordering before overlap checks. All planning, structural finalization, and span validation finish before any call to the external writer. Same-offset insertion ordering remains (start, end, seq).

Write::write_all preserves short-write, Interrupted, and WriteZero behavior. Errors are moved intact into WritePatchError::Io, and Error::source exposes the original std::io::Error including its custom payload. PatchError now implements Error so validation causes are also downcastable.

Existing public signatures, enum variants, exhaustive matching, and public struct construction remain unchanged. WritePatchError has the two fixed failure categories requested by the task; existing enums and structs were not marked non_exhaustive.

Malformed cloning template spans and empty template data are rejected with existing PatchError variants rather than indexing or subtraction panics. Valid template fragment allocation remains the existing planner behavior.

Documentation distinguishes validation atomicity from partial output after I/O failure. Integration tests compare every edit kind against buffered bytes, exercise late invalid and overlapping spans, test no writes or flushes on rejection, retain I/O payload identity, and verify direct borrowing for unchanged XML.
limitations: This was an isolated chart-component implementation; no full document engine or visual rendering validation was performed.
No allocation counts or performance benchmarks were measured. Direct input borrowing is tested for the no-edit case, and the streaming implementation was inspected for complete XML buffer allocation.
As with the existing API, ChartData must describe the same XML input. In-range coordinates alone cannot establish that provenance.
I/O failure may leave a prefix; no rollback guarantee is offered.
